claims.text: Mild thermal annealing under a reductive atmosphere can induce partial short-range ordering in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts without causing phase separation or significant sintering.
Partial short-range ordering produces fragmented nanodomains and enriched interfaces.
Short-range ordering can localize particular metals into compositionally enriched regions, including Pt-rich regions.
Partial short-range ordering shifts the catalyst's d-band electronic structure.
Short-range ordering changes the local coordination and electronic environment of catalytic sites.
Changes in local coordination and d-band position tune adsorption and desorption energetics of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Tuned adsorption and desorption energetics enhance catalytic turnover.
The annealing-induced structure minimizes catalyst deactivation by stabilizing active sites.
Fragmented domains with rich interfaces can improve catalytic performance by exposing more active sites.
Relative to an unannealed PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst, the annealed catalyst will have higher ethanol-oxidation current density.
Relative to the unannealed catalyst, the annealed catalyst will have a lower ethanol-oxidation onset potential.
The annealed catalyst may have greater durability than the unannealed catalyst.
The as-synthesized catalyst is uniformly mixed.
The unannealed baseline has a random atomic distribution with minimal short-range order.
The beneficial effect should occur only within a narrow annealing window that preserves nanoscale structural integrity and avoids phase separation and significant sintering.
STEM-EDX and FT-EXAFS can be used to detect elemental heterogeneity, short-range ordering, and domain formation in multielement nanoparticles.
The optimal degree of short-range ordering and the magnitude of its catalytic effect are unknown.
